title: Dermal Priming in Enhancing Vaccine Immunogenicity
off: Understanding the Impact of Local Dermal Priming in Enhancing Vaccine Immunogenicity in Patients Receiving B Cell Depleting Immunosuppression
sponsor: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
summary: Experimental medicine study in patients receiving B cell depletion therapy administering an immune challenge with seasonal influenza vaccination with/without concurrent administration of topical imiquimod (TLR7 agonist) aiming to determine proof of concept that local dermal immune priming alters physiological parameters following immunisation in this context.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosed with an autoimmune condition (including but not limited to ANCA associated vasculitis, IgG4 disease) and receiving B cell depletion therapy (eg, rituximab).
* Participant is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Has received immunosuppression in addition to rituximab in the last 3 months (oral prednisolone at any dose is permitted)
* Rituximab within less than 5 months or more than 18 months of screening
* Receiving oral prednisolone at a dose \> 5mg daily
* Has a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus or Sjogren's syndrome
* Is currently pregnant
* Has a recent history (documented, confirmed or suspected) of a flu-like illness within a week of vaccination
* Receiving anticoagulation (including warfarin, DOACs, clopidogrel, ticagrelor) for any indication or having any coagulation disorder. Low dose daily aspirin is permitted
* A known allergy or contraindications to imiquimod or influenza vaccine or excipients
* Prior vaccination with the current seasonal influenza vaccine
* Have any condition that the investigator believes may interfere with successful completion of the study

arms.l: Group 1: topical imiquimod (5% Aldara) + influenza vaccine
Group 3: topical imiquimod (5% Aldara) + saline (sham) vaccine

primary.m: Change in influenza-specific antibody neutralising capacity
